rows.body: Tagline: Think in Black & White Blu. Upper-upscale positioning for top urban and resort destinations—Nordic Nouveau design, Enticing Moments experience, Curatorial Warmth service. Americas presence: 10 open (3 domestic, 7 international)—confirm current counts and pipeline in your franchise disclosure. Loyalty: Choice Privileges under Choice-affiliated positioning.

Purpose fit: redefine upper-upscale hospitality—style with substance, innovation with comfort, belonging in an elevated environment. Operators who deliver design-forward full-service with gallery-curator service warmth and can run meetings, F&B theater, and tech-enabled guest rooms.

Top urban gateways, iconic resort markets, and design-forward conversions where guests expect memorable public spaces, fine-dining theater, and Scandinavian-inspired rooms—not limited-service or economy extended-stay.

Upper-upscale flag within the Choice portfolio—iconic design heritage (Arne Jacobsen lineage), distinctive public spaces, and enterprise distribution; above core Radisson upscale, not ultra-luxury or select-service.
New construction, adaptive reuse, and conversion where the asset can support upper-upscale casegoods, baths, and signature F&B—top urban and resort destinations per development criteria.

Radisson Blu balances upper-upscale design discipline—Nordic Nouveau interiors, memorable public spaces, and curatorial service warmth—with market-appropriate conversion paths. Iconic, stimulating environments should feel purposeful, not sterile; safety, cleanliness, and repeatable service benchmarks stay non-negotiable under Choice Privileges and portfolio QA where Choice-affiliated.

Design flexibility (detail): Prototype-driven with conversion paths—confirm design manual for your asset.

Conversion & development (detail): Conversion and new construction—confirm in your franchise disclosure document.

Localization (detail): Brand standards govern guest-facing consistency; limited localization of core guest touchpoints.

PIP / lifecycle capital (detail): PIP at opening, conversion, and renewal per agreement—sequence with financing.

Prototype dependence (detail): Design-forward prototype with local décor accents.

Radisson Blu is commonly paired with established third-party operators and franchisees in the Choice portfolio. Outcomes are strongest when the operator already runs upper-upscale or full-service assets and can implement portfolio systems, training, and QA cadence without service drift.

This brand is likely to be a better execution fit for operators comfortable balancing conversion pragmatism with structured brand expectations. It may be less suitable for lightly resourced operators without upper-upscale full-service depth.

Gateway and airport-adjacent repositioning where an independent or tired flag needs recognizable upper-upscale retail, corporate transient access, and a loyalty story guests already know.

Regional hub and secondary-city conversions where capex is measured and the owner wants portfolio distribution plus realistic standards—not a one-off soft brand.

Mixed corporate/leisure markets where weekend compression matters: the commercial plan should lean on brand.com and the active loyalty program in your market (Choice Privileges under Choice-affiliated positioning in many Americas markets; Radisson Blu Rewards where Radisson Blu Hotel Group program rules apply).

Conversion programs where a design-forward prototype mindset matters: varying layouts, room sizes, HVAC and bathroom configurations—with retention of viable elements where possible to protect speed and cost.

rows.title: Iconic Urban Flagship
rows.body: Strong fit where the owner wants a design-forward upper-upscale box in a top urban market—meetings, signature F&B, and Inspired Professional guests who reject boring big-box experiences.

rows.title: Resort and Leisure Destination
rows.body: Resort or mixed-use leisure settings where memorable public spaces, wellness, and distinctive design justify upper-upscale ADR—not a mainstream upscale conversion play.

rows.title: Adaptive Reuse and Conversion
rows.body: Adaptive reuse or conversion where structure and ceiling heights can support Blu public-space and room standards; pair with realistic capex and operator depth for gallery-curator service delivery.

Why owners choose Radisson Blu: upper-upscale design heritage with Choice distribution—style with substance for Inspired Professional travelers.

Guest promise: memorable public spaces, Nordic Nouveau rooms, and gallery-curator service warmth.

Three pillars: Enticing Moments (signature experiences and personalized service). Nordic Nouveau (distinctive design with modern comfort). Curatorial Warmth (welcoming, intuitive, upper-upscale hospitality).

Typical product: design-forward guest rooms; signature F&B and bar; meetings; fitness and wellness zones per prototype.

Your economics: gateway and resort destinations; design-forward prototype investment; upper-upscale labor and F&B. Loyalty per your FDD (Choice Privileges or Radisson Blu Rewards). Underwrite competitive set, capex, and net channel contribution.

Typical guest — Inspired Professional travelers who want distinctive design, efficient service, and authentic experiences—not generic big-box hotels.

What that means for you: guests expect Nordic Nouveau design, memorable public spaces, and reliable upscale service.

For owners and operators: expect clear upper-upscale standards, QA, and Choice distribution. Use the loyalty program name and rules in your franchise disclosure (Choice Privileges in many Americas agreements). Plan for casegoods, signature F&B, and gallery-curator service—not light conversion economics.

Radisson Blu’s operating profile fits owners who want CRS/brand.com participation, upper-upscale service standards, gallery-curator warmth, and loyalty-led direct contribution in markets where design-forward full-service is the right competitive set—not limited-service or core Radisson conversion economics.

Key differentiator — Beacon of Hospitality: rekindling upscale with heritage charm and timeless service; injecting soul back into every stay.

Experience — Enticing Moments: signature elements (e.g. classic diner) as the cornerstone of a personal atmosphere; every detail enhances the stay—from elevated amenities to personalized service—consistently unique and centered on what truly matters.

Design — Nordic Nouveau: rooted in American style and sensibility; classic hotel features reimagined with stylish, modern accents—intimately familiar.

Service — Curatorial Warmth: welcoming atmosphere, distinguished yet accessible; team embodies a trusted-bartender mindset—traditional hospitality with intuitive understanding of each guest’s needs.

Scalable upscale: airports, convention centers, resorts—not a single-lane boutique story. Journeymen tension: modern efficiency without the cold, interchangeable standardized-hotel feel.

Conversion discipline: design-forward prototype thinking for varied layouts, baths, and MEP — retain viable elements where it protects speed and cost.

Operational efficiency: maintainable guest rooms and right-sized F&B versus heavier full-service models that overbuild the kitchen.

Loyalty-led retail: pair brand.com and member constructs with the program name and rules in your disclosure (Choice Privileges vs Radisson Blu Rewards by market).

Commercial spine: CRS participation, structured standards, and QA rhythms owners can run repeatedly at scale — not campaign-only theater.

design-forward prototype conversion for varied layouts, baths, and MEP — retain viable elements where they protect speed and cost, then align casegoods, built-ins, and public areas so the upscale story matches the asset on opening day.
Markets where corporate midweek and leisure weekends both matter—the brand competes when compression is real through brand.com, transient retail, and loyalty aligned with your franchise agreement.

Speed-to-flag favors operators who can execute full-service standards without bespoke theater on every line item — clear QA cadence, repeatable service model, and sponsor reporting tied to contribution, not vanity awareness alone.

Guests get a distinctive upper-upscale stay built on Nordic Nouveau design, Enticing Moments service, and global brand recognition.

Owners gain Choice distribution, upper-upscale positioning, and a flag suited to gateway, resort, and CALA urban assets—not core Radisson conversion economics.

What you are buying: full-service upper-upscale operations; design-forward prototype investment; signature F&B and public-space capital; gallery-curator labor. Underwrite contribution after fees—loyalty, channel mix, and operating discipline versus your comp set.

Independent reflag: you need corporate access, upper-upscale positioning, and Choice Privileges where independents under-index on RFP and repeat stays.

Design-forward conversion: fits when public spaces, casegoods, and F&B can support Nordic Nouveau—not core Radisson conversion scope.

CALA gateway or resort: compare your asset to open Blu hotels in São Paulo, Santiago, Belo Horizonte Savassi, Bariloche, and Aruba for positioning—not as a guarantee of your returns.

Third-party operator: works when the operator can run upper-upscale F&B, meetings, and gallery-curator service without constant waivers.

Markets with weak corporate demand or one-season leisure need honest ramp and rate plans—no flag replaces geography.

Heavy capex conversions must align service model and meetings product with Radisson Blu standards early; late surprises compress ROI timelines.

Where OTAs dominate, owners should model net contribution after retail costs and member constructs—not headline RevPAR only.

Operator capability gaps show up in reviews and elite fulfillment first; solve staffing and training before leaning on campaigns.

Sponsor reporting: align KPIs to contribution, review trajectory, and direct mix—not vanity awareness metrics alone.

Screen market fit: compare your asset to open Blu hotels in Bariloche, São Paulo, Belo Horizonte Savassi, Santiago, and Aruba for positioning—not as a guarantee of your performance. Confirm Nordic Nouveau capex and staffing for your building and agreement.
Align Nordic Nouveau scope, meetings/F&B theater, and upper-upscale PIP with Alpha Brand Studios before major spend—sequence financing to prototype gates.
Pre-opening: gallery-curator hiring, Enticing Moments training, Choice systems cutover, and Think in Black & White Blu campaign readiness.
Opening: protect rate integrity and Blu service calibration (Enticing Moments, Nordic Nouveau rooms) in the first 90–120 days—CALA seasonality may differ from U.S. ramp curves.
Ramp: model Choice Privileges contribution, corporate accounts, and seasonality (urban vs resort). Benchmark against similar Blu markets if helpful—your ramp depends on local demand and execution.
Ongoing: upper-upscale capex cycles, Nordic Nouveau refresh, and contribution-focused benchmarking—Blu is not a logo swap from core Radisson.
Radisson Blu (Choice) · Choice Privileges® — loyalty at a glance

7,100+ hotels worldwide across 20+ brands; earn up to 10 points per $1 on eligible direct stays; reward nights from 8,000 points; Gold in 5 nights; Titanium top tier; Return & Earn and partner ecosystem—confirm chargeback and program rules in your FDD.

Model loyalty as net contribution—member discounts, fulfillment, and ~39.6% room mix from Choice Privileges in Item 19 sample (not headline RevPAR). Blu is upper-upscale—elite F&B recognition is a cost line, not optional.

rows.title: Campaign Scale
rows.body: U.S. News #1 hotel rewards program (consumer site, 14 programs evaluated); Return & Earn (1,000 pts after 2nd & 3rd qualifying stays/year)—pair with property execution.

Base earn: up to 10 points per $1 on qualifying stays booked direct at 7,100+ properties.
Fast Gold: 5 nights or 10,000 Elite Qualifying Credits (EQCs); cardholders can unlock Gold via Choice Privileges Mastercard spend.
Return & Earn: 1,000 bonus points after 2nd and 3rd qualifying stays each calendar year.
Cobrand: up to 16x–22x total points on stays with Choice Privileges Mastercard per choicehotels.com/choice-privileges.

Reward nights from 8,000 points (property and date dependent; demand-responsive pricing).
Points + cash where offered on eligible stays.
Partner redemptions (resorts, gift cards, airline miles, charity)—storytelling unless your FDD authorizes economics.

rows.body: Member — baseline rates, milestone rewards path, points never expire.

rows.body: Gold — 5 nights or 10,000 EQCs; bonus points on stays and enhanced recognition.

rows.title: Platinum
rows.body: Platinum — 15 nights or 30,000 EQCs; stronger earn bonus and elite benefits where available.

rows.title: Diamond
rows.body: Diamond — 35 nights or 70,000 EQCs; top mainstream tier with upgrades, late checkout, and milestone rewards where published.

rows.title: Titanium
rows.body: Titanium — 55 nights or 110,000 EQCs; highest published tier including Titanium Travel Award where offered.
Model net after distribution, member discounts, and redemption—strongest when direct/member mix supports your brand tier ADR; use Item 19 loyalty % where disclosed.
Elite recognition, welcome gifts, and breakfast/F&B promises at top tiers become labor and COGS—staff to brand standards before campaigns.
CRS/PMS loyalty integration and campaign tooling are mandatory—budget cutover, training, and choicehotels.com rate parity discipline.

Radisson Blu is most compelling for owners targeting top urban and resort destinations who want recognizable upper-upscale design heritage, Choice distribution, and loyalty-led retail for the Inspired Professional—guests allergic to boring, big-box experiences. Strongest with operators who can deliver design-forward F&B, meetings product, and gallery-curator service without waivers. Weaker where the physical plant cannot support upper-upscale casegoods and public-space investment, or where the market is better served by core Radisson upscale conversion economics.
